question: A 43-year-old woman visits her primary care provider complaining of fatigue. Although she has had it for several months, her fatigue has been worsening over the past few weeks. She has no other symptoms. Past medical history is significant for hypertension. She takes chlorthalidone, an oral contraceptive pill, and a multivitamin every day. Family history is noncontributory. She drinks about 1 bottle of wine every day and started taking a shot or two of whisky or vodka every morning before work to “clear out the cobwebs”. She was recently fired from her job. Today, her heart rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 17/min, blood pressure is 110/65 mm Hg, and temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F). On physical exam, she appears malnourished and anxious. Her conjunctiva are pale, and glossitis is noted on oral exam. Her heart has a regular rate and rhythm and her lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. She has no gait or balance abnormalities. Lab results show a hemoglobin of 10 g/dL, with a mean corpuscular volume (MCV) of 108 fl. Elevated level of which of the following will most likely to be found in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Alcohol consumption -> impaired absorption of essential nutrients -> malnutrition -> glossitis and pale conjunctiva -> macrocytic anemia with elevated MCV -> elevated Methylmalonic acid -> 85%
CHAIN: Alcohol abuse -> decreased folate and vitamin B12 levels -> impaired DNA synthesis -> ineffective erythropoiesis -> macrocytic anemia with elevated MCV -> elevated Homocysteine -> 80%
enhanced_information: Alcohol abuse can lead to decreased folate and vitamin B12 levels, impairing DNA synthesis and causing macrocytic anemia with elevated MCV. This patient's presentation of glossitis, pale conjunctiva, and macrocytic anemia with an elevated MCV suggests a deficiency in vitamin B12, leading to elevated Homocysteine levels. Therefore, the most likely elevated substance in this patient is Homocysteine (opb).
analysis: The patient presents with macrocytic anemia (elevated MCV) and symptoms suggestive of vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, such as glossitis and fatigue. Her alcohol use and malnourished appearance further support the possibility of a nutritional deficiency. Both vitamin B12 and folate deficiencies can lead to elevated homocysteine levels. However, only vitamin B12 deficiency would also elevate methylmalonic acid levels. Given the absence of neurological symptoms, folate deficiency is more likely, which would result in elevated homocysteine levels.
